findings.text: Test program builder for register-to-register arithmetic and logic coverage. Given an operation selector and a width selector, it allocates a program buffer, chooses width-appropriate seed operands, derives expected outcomes including the same-register case, then emits one self-verifying block per ordered destination and source register pair over the general register set. The completed program and its length are stored into the supplied test descriptor.

Twelve narrow adapters each fix the operation selector to one move, logic, shift, or arithmetic meaning while fixing the width selector to full width, delegating all construction to the shared pair generator and returning its status unchanged.

Twelve narrow adapters each fix the operation selector to one move, logic, shift, or arithmetic meaning while fixing the width selector to narrow width, delegating all construction to the shared pair generator and returning its status unchanged.

For shift meanings the source seed is constrained to a small range, and for narrow width the expected values are truncated to their low half. Each emitted block checks both the low portion and the high portion of the destination, with mismatch causing early termination carrying a diagnostic marker and full traversal reaching a success marker.

Two fixed-size emitters build self-checking atomic update tests for doubleword and word widths. Each supports a sizing query when no output buffer is supplied, distinguishes exchange from read-modify-write meanings and fetch from non-fetch variants, preserves a sentinel register to detect clobbering, and validates updated memory plus the source register outcome against precomputed expectations.

Two fixed-size emitters build compare-and-swap tests that first exercise a mismatched comparison and then a matched comparison, checking both memory contents and the comparison register after each attempt. The narrow-width form accounts for verifier-inserted zero extension and uses a longer sequence with an extra reload between attempts.

The doubleword atomic suite shares one width-specific forwarder to the common pattern filler with its atomic emitter. Per-meaning adapters select among four read-modify-write meanings, their fetch forms, and exchange, while the compare-and-swap adapter bypasses that forwarder and reaches the pattern filler directly with its own emitter and no operation context.

The word atomic suite shares one width-specific forwarder to the common pattern filler with its atomic emitter. Per-meaning adapters select among four read-modify-write meanings, their fetch forms, and exchange, while the compare-and-swap adapter bypasses that forwarder and reaches the pattern filler directly with its own emitter and no operation context.

Exhaustive register-pair atomic program builder parameterized by memory width and operation. It uses width-specific memory and update seeds, precomputes the expected post-update memory value with distinct treatment for exchange and compare-and-swap, then emits one self-checking block per ordered address and data register pair covering the comparison register, source register, address register, and memory under aliasing rules, ending with a success marker.
Ten thin adapters fix memory width to doubleword and each fix a distinct atomic meaning including fetch variants, exchange, and compare-and-swap, delegating to the shared register-pair builder.
Ten thin adapters fix memory width to word and each fix a distinct atomic meaning including fetch variants, exchange, and compare-and-swap, delegating to the shared register-pair builder.

Wide immediate loader test builder sweeping magnitude boundaries. It covers low bit positions with a neighbourhood around each power of two in both polarities, emitting for each value a load together with an independently constructed reference and an equality check that ends early on mismatch, bracketed by initial failure and final success markers.

Wide immediate loader test builder sweeping byte-composition patterns. It enumerates all per-byte choices between two masked random-influenced byte sources, evolves a deterministic generator per pattern, and emits for each resulting constant a load plus an independently built reference and equality check with early termination on mismatch, bracketed by failure and success markers.

Four thin adapters configure the byte-composition builder with distinct base and mask pairs to emphasize alternating full-byte values, sign-bit variations, positive-versus-zero mixing, and negative-versus-zero mixing.

Builders that allocate their own program buffer report allocation exhaustion with a negative out-of-memory status without touching the test descriptor. On success they install the buffer pointer and length into the descriptor pointer union and return zero.

After construction each self-allocating builder asserts that internal length accounting matches the allocated or used size. A violation signals an internal sizing miscalculation rather than an input-dependent failure.
Ordered register-pair coverage spans ten general registers from the zero register through the ninth register, yielding one hundred ordered pairs per operation and width.

Sizing queries for the atomic and compare-and-swap emitters return fixed instruction counts: doubleword atomic and word atomic each twenty-one, doubleword compare-and-swap twenty-three, word compare-and-swap twenty-seven.
Atomic checks address memory through the frame pointer with an eight-byte slot for doubleword width and a four-byte slot for word width.

Generated programs behave as a linear chain of guarded blocks: each block either terminates early with a failure indication on first mismatch or falls through, and traversing all blocks reaches a terminal success indication. Emitters given a null buffer perform no writes and only report their fixed size.
